title: MemHarness — code view
subtitle: What the training/eval code actually executes: cold-start SFT feeds a shared policy that decides queries, retrieves, reconstructs via a memory adaptor, then acts. Lane = canonical stage (METHODOLOGY-SKELETON §2.2); B3/B5 are the only empty lanes, same as the paper view.
source: KnowledgeXLab/MemHarness @ 31329e8   ·   every file.py:NNN re-opened and confirmed during verification (servers/memharness/verification.md §4)
legend_notes: Cold-start SFT (scripts/cold_start_sft.sh: 2 epoch / lr 1e-5 / eff. batch 2) is real and matches the paper's numbers exactly — both original architecture docs missed this entire phase; drawn here as in the paper view.

Headline divergence: under the config both training scripts use (use_actor_rollout_wg=true), train_memory_adaptor_enabled() returns False (mem_adaptor_training.py:336-337) -> the reconstruction completion never enters any gradient update (ray_trainer.py:1890 skips the whole block) -- contradicts §3.4's 'shared credit across thinking/reconstruction/action' claim.

Reconstruction still fires on zero-hit turns: the empty_retrieval_message injection makes `injected` truthy, so maybe_apply_memory_adaptor runs even with nothing retrieved (mem_adaptor_rollout.py:192-207,636-640) -- there is no 'skip if nothing retrieved' branch anywhere.

Several base-config defaults are silently overridden by both training scripts and were mistaken for code defaults in the original docs: experience_summarizer.mode base is 'none' (writes nothing) not 'self'; prune_score_threshold base is 0.35 not 0.3; prune_every_n_global_steps base is 0 (pruning off); retrieval_mode base is 'fixed' (unconditional, no LLM decision) not 'agentic'; Milvus schema is 19 fields not 18.
